text: A small café. Its AI coworkers run the money. You approve. PayPal moves it.
Try it yourself in one click, at rays dot to. You land in a demo café, signed in as its manager, with fourteen live demos.

At closing time, the close agent asks PayPal's MCP server for the day's transactions. This Sandbox app doesn't have that list switched on yet, so the agent says so and reconciles from Raysto's own record of PayPal captures, refunds and cash. You sign off; nothing is posted until you do.

Pay the team. This week's clocked shifts become wages, and the tip pool is split by hours and role, as one batch. After your identity check, PayPal Payouts sends it to each person's PayPal, and the batch id is kept.

A customer asks for lunch for twelve. The catering agent prices it from the menu, keeps to the budget, and drafts a PayPal invoice with a deposit. One approval sends it through PayPal Invoicing, with a QR code the customer pays from.

A customer asks for lunch for twelve. The catering agent prices it from the menu, keeps to the budget, and drafts a PayPal invoice with a deposit. The moment the Sandbox app has Invoicing switched on, one approval sends it through PayPal Invoicing, with a QR code to pay from.

A diner says their wrap was missing. The complaints agent reads the kitchen ticket and PayPal's capture through MCP, and proposes a partial refund with its reasons. Your identity check approves it; PayPal refunds, and the refund id lands on the order.
When a diner walks away from PayPal, the payments agent asks PayPal itself through the MCP server, shows that evidence, and drafts the release. Nothing moves without you.
Diners order in one sentence. Raysto builds a priced basket from the real menu; one tap places the order and opens PayPal's own page.
The payment is captured once, on the server, and the ticket goes straight to the kitchen.

A bill arrives as a PDF. The accountant reads it with Gemini: vendor, amount, tax and due date. It matches last month's bill from the same utility, finds the utility's PayPal account there, and checks this bill was never paid before. After your identity check, PayPal Payouts pays it, and the batch id lands on the bill.
Every capture, refund, fee, payout and bill becomes one double-entry journal. The accountant reads the month, profit and loss and tax, and explains anything odd with the PayPal id it is about.
Money the café is owed works the same way. A catering deposit becomes a PayPal pay link with a QR code. The customer pays on PayPal's page, and the capture marks it paid in the books.

Delivery apps plug in through Raysto's Delivery Partner API. Here a labelled simulator sends a signed order. The AI dispatcher ranks the café's drivers by distance and load; you approve the offer, and the partner gets a signed webhook at every step.

Supplies don't run out. From four weeks of sales and the recipes, Raysto sees what runs out before the next delivery. The supply planner drafts the order up to par and flags a price that moved; when the goods arrive, the order, the delivery note and the bill are matched three ways.
An owner with two cafés sees both in one AG Studio view: profit and loss by café and month, from the same journal. An area manager can read it; paying anything still needs that café's own approval.
The same coworkers read a printed menu into the system, hear an order at the counter, and draw a dish for the menu. Every one of them waits for a person to approve.

AI coworkers on PayPal Orders, Payouts, Refunds, Invoicing, Transactions and Disputes, through PayPal's MCP server. The payouts, the refund and the captures you saw ran live in Sandbox, with their ids on screen.
AI coworkers run the café's money. You approve. PayPal moves it. Try Raysto at rays dot to.
